packet.headline_seed: Extreme heat continues in central and eastern Europe with temperatures of 38C expected – Europe live
packet.description_seed: Germany, Czechia, Poland and Hungary reached record temperatures of more than 40C on Sunday Record-high temperatures were also recorded in Germany over the weekend, with reports of wildfires and Berlin police resorting to using water cannons to cool down the crowds. clean_source_blocks.text: An extreme heat warning has been expanded as the UK braces for a heatwave that could send temperatures soaring to a record-breaking 38C. The Met Office said London could see highs of 38C on Wednesday and Thursday, adding that there is "growing confidence" that this week could break the record for the hottest June temperature of 35.6C, set in 1976 in Southampton. The hot weather, which is expected to last until at least Thursday, has sparked weather warnings, health alerts and concerns for vulnerable people. An amber extreme heat warning issued by the Met Office has been extended to last from Monday until Thursday. Monday and Tuesday’s warning covers most of southern England, central and eastern Wales, and much of the Midlands, while Wednesday and Thursday’s alert also includes parts of Greater Manchester, Yorkshire and Cheshire.

For the second time in two months, western and central Europe has been hit by a record-breaking heatwave. Temperature records have toppled in multiple countries, with France seeing its “hottest day ever” for two days running and the UK, Spain and Switzerland breaking records for June. A rapid-response attribution study has concluded that “climate change is unequivocally to blame”, noting that the scorching temperatures would have been “virtually impossible” 50 years ago. The research also found that the sweltering overnight temperatures seen this week are “100 times” more likely today than they were in 2003 when Europe was hit by a deadly summer heatwave. The extreme conditions come on the 50th anniversary of a historic 1976 heatwave in the UK, prompting many comparisons of the two events from scientists and the media.

The weather service has warned people of the risks of open-water swimming, such as cold water shock. During a hot spell in May, 17 people - most of them teenagers - died in open-water incidents across South Yorkshire, West Yorkshire, Cornwall, Hampshire, Warwickshire, Cheshire, Pembrokeshire, Lincolnshire and Lancashire. Meanwhile, much of Europe is also sweltering under the heatwave, with temperatures forecast to hit 37C in Rome and 39C in Madrid on Monday. In France, highs of 40C are expected on Sunday, with Monday likely to be even hotter as emergency services and military forces have been put on wildfire alert. The climate crisis is making extreme weather events - such as heatwaves, floods, droughts and storms - increasingly common across the world. A Met ---

In Rome, pilgrims in St Peter’s Square used parasols and umbrellas to shield themselves from the blazing sun as the Pope led a traditional Sunday prayer from a window of the Apostolic Palace. The spike in temperatures is being driven by a mass of hot air moving north from the Sahara, fuelled by a strong high‑pressure system known as the “African anticyclone.” Italy, Spain, France and the U.K. baked on Sunday as the recent heat wave intensified and temperatures climbed to 40 Celsius. Meteorologists say the system is creating a so‑called “heat dome,” trapping hot air over western and central Europe and allowing temperatures to build day after day. Madrid residents and tourists used fans and drank plenty of cold drinks as they browsed the city’s famous El Rastro flea market.

Italy, Spain, France and the U.K. baked on Sunday as the recent heat wave intensified and temperatures climbed to 40 Celsius.

Meteorologists say the system is creating a so‑called “heat dome,” trapping hot air over western and central Europe and allowing temperatures to build day after day.

Madrid residents and tourists used fans and drank plenty of cold drinks as they browsed the city’s famous El Rastro flea market.

“I’m dressed all in white because it’s so hot, and I’m carrying my little electric fan everywhere I go,” said Haily San Cesario, a 22-year-old engineer from Miami.

payload.title: Helleaalto kiristyy Länsi- ja Keski-Euroopassa
payload.summary: Länsi- ja Keski-Eurooppaa koettelee jälleen poikkeuksellinen helleaalto, jonka aikana lämpötilojen ennustetaan nousevan paikoin lähelle tai yli 40 astetta. Britanniassa viranomaiset ovat laajentaneet äärimmäisen kuumuuden varoituksia, ja Etelä-Euroopassa kuumuus on lisännyt huolta maastopaloista ja terveysriskeistä.
payload.content:
Länsi- ja Keski-Euroopassa jatkuva helleaalto on nostamassa lämpötiloja poikkeuksellisen korkeiksi useissa maissa, ja viranomaiset varoittavat sekä terveysriskeistä että maastopalojen vaarasta. Britanniassa Lontoon lämpötilan arvioidaan voivan nousta keskiviikkona ja torstaina 38 asteeseen, samalla kun Italiassa, Espanjassa ja Ranskassa on mitattu tai ennustettu jopa 40 asteen lukemia.

## Varoituksia laajennettiin Britanniassa

Britannian ilmatieteen laitos on laajentanut keltaista vakavampaa, oranssia äärimmäisen kuumuuden varoitusta maanantaista torstaihin. Maanantain ja tiistain varoitus koskee suurta osaa Etelä-Englannista, Keski- ja Itä-Walesia sekä laajoja alueita Midlandsissa. Keskiviikkona ja torstaina varoitusalue ulottuu myös osiin Suur-Manchesteria, Yorkshirea ja Cheshirea.

Lontoon ennustetaan voivan yltää 38 asteeseen viikon puolivälissä. Viranomaisten mukaan on kasvavaa varmuutta siitä, että Britannian kesäkuun lämpöennätys voi rikkoutua. Nykyinen ennätys on 35,6 astetta, joka mitattiin Southamptonissa vuonna 1976.

Kuumuus on herättänyt huolta erityisesti haavoittuvassa asemassa olevista ihmisistä. Lisäksi viranomaiset ovat muistuttaneet avovesiuinnin vaaroista, kuten kylmäshokista. Toukokuun lämpimän jakson aikana Britanniassa kuoli 17 ihmistä avovesionnettomuuksissa, ja suurin osa uhreista oli teini-ikäisiä.

## Kuuma ilma kerääntyy Euroopan ylle

Meteorologien mukaan lämpötilojen nousua ajaa Saharasta pohjoiseen virtaava kuuma ilmamassa, jota vahvistaa voimakas korkeapaine. Ilmiö vangitsee kuumaa ilmaa Länsi- ja Keski-Euroopan ylle ja antaa lämpötilojen nousta päivä päivältä.

Roomassa lämpötilan ennustettiin nousevan maanantaina 37 asteeseen ja Madridissa 39 asteeseen. Ranskassa odotettiin sunnuntaina 40 asteen lukemia, ja maanantain arvioitiin olevan vielä kuumempi. Pelastusviranomaiset ja asevoimat on asetettu Ranskassa valmiuteen maastopalojen riskin vuoksi.

Tutkijoiden mukaan Euroopan viimeaikainen kuumuus liittyy ilmastonmuutoksen voimistamaan äärevään säähän. Tuoreen pikamallinnukseen perustuvan arvion mukaan tämänkaltaiset polttavat lämpötilat olisivat olleet käytännössä mahdottomia 50 vuotta sitten. Samassa arviossa todetaan, että tukalat yölämpötilat ovat nykyisin noin sata kertaa todennäköisempiä kuin vuoden 2003 tuhoisan hellekesän aikaan.
summary_bullets: Länsi- ja Keski-Euroopassa lämpötilat nousevat paikoin lähelle tai yli 40 astetta.
Britanniassa äärimmäisen kuumuuden varoitusta on laajennettu maanantaista torstaihin.
Viranomaiset varoittavat terveysriskeistä, avovesiuinnin vaaroista ja maastopalojen uhasta.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu packetin neljään lähdeblokkiin. Saksaa ja Itä-Euroopan yksityiskohtia ei käytetty, koska valitut lähdeblokit eivät tukeneet niitä riittävästi.

Meteorologien mukaan lämpötilojen nousua ajaa Saharasta pohjoiseen virtaava kuuma ilmamassa, jota vahvistaa voimakas korkeapaine. Ilmiö vangitsee kuumaa ilmaa Länsi- ja Keski-Euroopan ylle ja antaa lämpötilojen nousta päivä päivältä.

Roomassa lämpötilan ennustettiin nousevan maanantaina 37 asteeseen ja Madridissa 39 asteeseen. Ranskassa odotettiin sunnuntaina 40 asteen lukemia, ja maanantain arvioitiin olevan vielä kuumempi. Pelastusviranomaiset ja asevoimat on asetettu Ranskassa valmiuteen maastopalojen riskin vuoksi.

Tutkijoiden mukaan Euroopan viimeaikainen kuumuus liittyy ilmastonmuutoksen voimistamaan äärevään säähän. Tuoreen pikamallinnukseen perustuvan arvion mukaan tämänkaltaiset polttavat lämpötilat olisivat olleet käytännössä mahdottomia 50 vuotta sitten. Samassa arviossa todetaan, että tukalat yölämpötilat ovat nykyisin noin sata kertaa todennäköisempiä kuin vuoden 2003 tuhoisan hellekesän aikaan.

An extreme heat warning has been expanded as the UK braces for a heatwave that could send temperatures soaring to a record-breaking 38C. The Met Office said London could see highs of 38C on Wednesday and Thursday, adding that there is "growing confidence" that this week could break the record for the hottest June temperature of 35.6C, set in 1976 in Southampton. The hot weather, which is expected to last until at least Thursday, has sparked weather warnings, health alerts and concerns for vulnerable people. An amber extreme heat warning issued by the Met Office has been extended to last from Monday until Thursday. Monday and Tuesday’s warning covers most of southern England, central and eastern Wales, and much of the Midlands, while Wednesday and Thursday’s alert also includes parts of Greater Manchester, Yorkshire and Cheshire.

For the second time in two months, western and central Europe has been hit by a record-breaking heatwave. Temperature records have toppled in multiple countries, with France seeing its “hottest day ever” for two days running and the UK, Spain and Switzerland breaking records for June. A rapid-response attribution study has concluded that “climate change is unequivocally to blame”, noting that the scorching temperatures would have been “virtually impossible” 50 years ago. The research also found that the sweltering overnight temperatures seen this week are “100 times” more likely today than they were in 2003 when Europe was hit by a deadly summer heatwave. The extreme conditions come on the 50th anniversary of a historic 1976 heatwave in the UK, prompting many comparisons of the two events from scientists and the media.

The weather service has warned people of the risks of open-water swimming, such as cold water shock. During a hot spell in May, 17 people - most of them teenagers - died in open-water incidents across South Yorkshire, West Yorkshire, Cornwall, Hampshire, Warwickshire, Cheshire, Pembrokeshire, Lincolnshire and Lancashire. Meanwhile, much of Europe is also sweltering under the heatwave, with temperatures forecast to hit 37C in Rome and 39C in Madrid on Monday. In France, highs of 40C are expected on Sunday, with Monday likely to be even hotter as emergency services and military forces have been put on wildfire alert. The climate crisis is making extreme weather events - such as heatwaves, floods, droughts and storms - increasingly common across the world. A Met ---

In Rome, pilgrims in St Peter’s Square used parasols and umbrellas to shield themselves from the blazing sun as the Pope led a traditional Sunday prayer from a window of the Apostolic Palace. The spike in temperatures is being driven by a mass of hot air moving north from the Sahara, fuelled by a strong high‑pressure system known as the “African anticyclone.” Italy, Spain, France and the U.K. baked on Sunday as the recent heat wave intensified and temperatures climbed to 40 Celsius. Meteorologists say the system is creating a so‑called “heat dome,” trapping hot air over western and central Europe and allowing temperatures to build day after day. Madrid residents and tourists used fans and drank plenty of cold drinks as they browsed the city’s famous El Rastro flea market.
